summary:
Vivek Muppalla of Hippocratic AI describes building an AI system for proactive patient outreach, with over 200M clinical conversations deployed across 60+ health systems and zero significant safety incidents. He frames healthcare as a scarcity problem and motivates the work with a live patient call covering drug name spelling (prazosin), vital sign clarification, medication stoppage (nifedipine), and nurse escalation.

Muppalla argues that off-the-shelf voice stacks cannot satisfy clinical safety because accurate models take tens of seconds while fast models are unsafe. Hippocratic therefore built a vertically integrated stack that is three times faster than competitors at P99 latency. The system's three stages are hearing, reasoning, and speaking, with the reasoning layer organized as the Polaris constellation: 31 models run in parallel per conversation, including one central conversation model and 30 specialists (labs, medications, scheduling). Specialists first do a fast check to decide whether they need to speak, short-circuiting when they do not; the central model then integrates any specialist input while staying within the latency budget. Asynchronous verifier models run in the background to validate tool-call parameters and responses, achieving 99.49% accuracy on scheduling. For use cases with extra budget, offline verifiers catch errors post hoc so the team can course-correct or call patients back.

Inference is treated as a quality-constrained, speed-optimization problem. Three lossless optimizations are highlighted: four-bit quantization shrinking model math from 16-bit to 4-bit, speculative decoding with a smaller model pre-generating tokens for the main model to check, and a KV cache compression system that keeps long conversations warm, yielding an over 96% cache hit rate and an 18x speedup on pre-fill.

Evaluation is treated as a statistical and clinical problem. With 10,000 calls per day, a 1% failure rate on scheduling means 100 patients per day get the wrong appointment, and worse, could miss a critical one. Catching a 1% error statistically requires about 450 tests, and seeing it ten times requires about 1,900. Pure synthetic data is insufficient, so Hippocratic uses over 7,000 trained clinicians who have graded close to 800,000 conversations.

Safety is graded on the same rubric used for humans: correctness, no harm, minor harm, severe harm, death. Across five product generations, Polaris reaches 99.89% no-harm accuracy versus roughly 81% for humans on the same scale. Beyond safety, Hippocratic built HEART, a public empathy benchmark, because people must want to talk to the system, not just tolerate it. Muppalla closes by noting that hiring, residency programs, and unlimited tokens reflect an AI-native culture, and that Hippocratic refused to trade off quality, speed, and safety.

sections.title: Opening framing and the oath
sections.summary: Muppalla introduces Hippocratic AI, the scarcity framing of healthcare, and the oath of 'do no harm, patient first, access for all.' Audience is asked if they have received a proactive call; almost no hands go up.

sections.title: Scale and product demonstration
sections.summary: Claims of 200M interactions, zero significant safety incidents, 60+ deployments, 8.5/10 satisfaction, followed by a live demo covering identity confusion, prazosin spelling, blood pressure/heart rate confirmation, nifedipine stoppage, and nurse escalation.

sections.title: Intelligence vs. latency and the vertical stack
sections.summary: Argues that accurate models are too slow and fast models too unsafe, justifying a vertically integrated stack. Latency wins are reinvested in intelligence as a compounding flywheel, with >99% accuracy required on lab-results and IVR benchmarks.

sections.title: Polaris constellation architecture
sections.summary: Introduces the three-stage system: hearing, reasoning, and speaking. The brain runs 31 models in parallel, with one central conversation model and 30 specialists (labs, medications, scheduling), avoiding a single point of failure.

sections.title: Decoder-only audio LLM for ASR
sections.summary: Describes Whisper V3 fine-tuned on millions of clinical conversations, conformer projector preserving prosody, contextual biasing with finite medication lists, and secondary scoring for single-word answers to cut medical word error rate by over 50%.

sections.title: Parallel orchestration, verifiers, and inference optimizations
sections.summary: Explains that specialists short-circuit when they have nothing to say, the central model integrates their input, and asynchronous verifiers validate tool-call parameters to reach 99.49% scheduling accuracy. Three lossless inference optimizations are detailed: 4-bit quantization, speculative decoding, and KV cache compression achieving over 96% hit rate and 18x pre-fill speedup, with P99 latency three times faster than competitors.

sections.title: Statistical evaluation, human-harm grading, and HEART empathy
sections.summary: Argues that 99% accuracy on 10,000 daily calls means 100 wrong appointments and is unacceptable; catching a 1% failure requires ~450 tests and ~1,900 to see it ten times. Evaluation blends synthetic data with 7,000+ trained clinicians who graded close to 800,000 conversations. Safety is graded on the human clinical rubric (correctness, no harm, minor harm, severe harm, death), with Polaris at 99.89% no-harm vs. ~81% for humans. HEART is introduced as a public empathy benchmark, and the talk closes with AI-native hiring, residency programs, unlimited tokens, and the refusal to trade off quality, speed, and safety.

organization.name: Hippocratic AI
organization.summary: Hippocratic AI is an independent Palo Alto company that builds safety-focused healthcare voice agents. Its first-party site describes a clinical-abundance mission, values of do-no-harm and patient-first, and Polaris, a patented constellation of a primary conversational model plus specialist supervisors. Official product and engineering pages document Polaris 5.0, custom clinical ASR, and production scale of hundreds of millions of patient interactions with clinician-graded safety. Vivek Muppalla, VP of Engineering, is the speaker and an implementation author of the voice-stack posts.
organization.status: Independent company as of the research date. Homepage, about page, Polaris product pages, and engineering blog are live. Polaris 5.0 is the current generation. No ownership change since the August 2026 talk.

evidence.excerpt: These models are fantastic at what they do. They're clinically safe. But unfortunately, many of these models take tens of seconds to respond, sometimes over a minute.

evidence.excerpt: We in fact run 31 models at any given point of time for every conversation. So, we have one central model ... where we have other 30 specialist models
most of what looks like model reasoning failures end up actually being model mishearing things

evidence.excerpt: it also maintains all the prosody. So, all the pauses and the stresses are maintained. So, the model hears not just the what, but also the how.
evidence.supports: Conformer projector preserves prosody so the model hears how things are said.

evidence.excerpt: when a patient mentions a medication name, we aren't guessing from like an infinite list of medications, but we have the chance to optimize around a finite list
evidence.supports: Contextual biasing against a finite medication list improves accuracy.

evidence.supports: Single-word mishears are catastrophic, motivating secondary rescoring.

evidence.supports: Hippocratic stack is 3x faster at P99 latency.
